title: Session Risk Memory (SRM): Temporal Authorization for Deterministic Pre-Execution Safety Gates

object.carrier: Session Risk Memory: a compact semantic centroid representing the evolving behavioral profile of an agent session, plus a risk signal accumulated through an exponential moving average over baseline-subtracted gate outputs; both operate on the same semantic vector representation as the underlying deterministic gate, with no additional model components, training, or probabilistic inference; the state lives and is evaluated over the trajectory of one session

safety_property.statement: Temporal authorization consistency: individually-compliant steps that collectively decompose harmful intent (slow-burn exfiltration, gradual privilege escalation, compliance drift) must be caught at the trajectory level, not only per action. Failure condition of the baseline being extended: stateless per-action gates are 'structurally blind to distributed attacks that decompose harmful intent across multiple individually-compliant steps'. Judged by F1, false positive rate, and detection rate over multi-turn attack sessions, with per-turn overhead as the cost side.
safety_property.operationalized_as: F1, FPR, and detection rate on a multi-turn benchmark of 80 sessions containing slow-burn exfiltration, gradual privilege escalation, and compliance drift scenarios; SRM extends the ILION gate and is compared against stateless ILION; per-turn overhead in microseconds.

capabilities: Distributed attack: decomposes harmful intent across multiple individually-compliant steps, each of which passes deterministic per-action authorization (spatial authorization consistency holds per action while the trajectory violates temporal authorization consistency)
Attack scenarios evaluated: slow-burn exfiltration, gradual privilege escalation, and compliance drift across multi-turn sessions
assumptions: A deterministic pre-execution safety gate (ILION) already evaluates each agent action against assigned roles; SRM extends it with trajectory-level authorization using the same semantic vector representation
Per the abstract, SRM requires no additional model components, training, or probabilistic inference
not_covered: The full paper (threat-model section, adversary knowledge assumptions, additional baselines and analyses) was not accessible for this card - no HTML full text exists on arXiv or ar5iv; all card content is grounded in the abstract only
Adaptive attackers that probe or evade the temporal risk signal are not addressed in the abstract

intervention.name: Session Risk Memory (SRM): trajectory-level authorization module on top of a deterministic per-action gate
intervention.description: A lightweight deterministic module extending stateless pre-execution safety gates with trajectory-level (temporal) authorization: it maintains a compact semantic centroid tracking the session's evolving behavioral profile and accumulates a risk signal via exponential moving average over baseline-subtracted gate outputs, reusing the gate's semantic vector representation; the framework distinguishes spatial authorization consistency (per action) from temporal authorization consistency (over trajectory).

results.claim: On a multi-turn benchmark of 80 sessions (slow-burn exfiltration, gradual privilege escalation, compliance drift), ILION+SRM achieves F1 = 1.0000 with 0% false positive rate vs stateless ILION at F1 = 0.9756 with 5% FPR, both maintaining a 100% detection rate.
results.metric: F1 / FPR / detection rate on the 80-session multi-turn benchmark
results.value: F1 1.0000 (SRM) vs 0.9756 (stateless ILION); FPR 0% vs 5%; detection 100% both
results.setting: Multi-turn benchmark of 80 sessions with slow-burn exfiltration, gradual privilege escalation, and compliance drift scenarios (per abstract)
results.quote: Results show that ILION+SRM achieves F1 = 1.0000 with 0% false positive rate, compared to stateless ILION at F1 = 0.9756 with 5% FPR, while maintaining 100% detection rate for both systems.

denominator.how_counted: Metrics over the 80 multi-turn attack sessions of the benchmark; per-session turn counts and per-scenario splits are not stated in the abstract

results.claim: Cost reading: SRM eliminates all false positives with a per-turn overhead under 250 microseconds - the temporal-authorization state is cheap enough for pre-execution gating.
results.comparison: added on top of the underlying deterministic gate, with no additional model components or training
results.setting: SRM module operating on the same semantic vector representation as the underlying gate (per abstract)
results.quote: Critically, SRM eliminates all false positives with a per-turn overhead under 250 microseconds.

denominator.how_counted: Per-turn overhead measured across the benchmark sessions; measurement methodology is not stated in the abstract
